MonitoringProgramDescription:
Lake Tahoe's surface rises with snowmelt and falls through dry years. Below the natural rim, 6,223 feet, no water flows out into the Truckee River. Above it, the dam at Tahoe City holds the lake no higher than the legal limit of 6,229.1 feet.

A warmer climate shifts precipitation from snow to rain and lengthens droughts, which makes the swings between full and low lake more extreme.
MonitoringApproach: The U.S. Geological Survey gauges the lake level at Tahoe City. The chart shows the weekly mean against the natural rim and the legal limit.
